correctness.rationale: The support-function formula is exact for each coordinate-plane disk. Gaussian polar independence gives (1) with all edge-pair covariances explicitly classified; tree degree-excess inequalities prove unique sharp extremizers. A one-dependent bivariate central limit theorem plus radial delta method proves the path Gaussian limit. Conditional strong law yields the star limit, and explicit small-argument integration yields the logarithmic edge constant. The actual verify.py was run successfully on 20 finite graph cases and all 18,247 Prüfer-labeled trees of orders 3–7; no finite test is substituted for a proof.

value.rationale: The work supplies an exact graph-invariant spherical width variance for curved, graph-indexed zonoids, proves globally unique path/star tree extremizers, and shows a sharp change from constant-scale Gaussian path widths to square-root-scale non-Gaussian star widths. The star limit has a novel, explicit logarithmic suppression of its lower-edge probability, which is absent in the closest line-segment analogue. The claimed invariant and boundary effect are natural objects of convex-body width statistics, not arbitrary finite slices.
